page: Amazon Web Services d3en.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance tailored for data-dense architectures requiring vast local capacity alongside high network throughput. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz across the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores with two threads per core), 35 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions. Memory is configured with 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not include GPU acceleration.

Storage and networking are the primary differentiators of the d3en.8xlarge. The system bundles 223,680 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity directly on the instance, combined with a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate that compute performance aligns with standard multithreaded capacity, delivering a PassMark CPU score of 26,401.64 and Geekbench multicore score of 10,098.0. However, single-threaded processing remains limited, registering in the bottom quartile across stress-ng (1,327.88) and single-core Geekbench (1,120.0). Memory throughput scales reliably under uncached read tests at 109.98 GB/sec and uncached writes at 48.04 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance delivers high resource density for workloads demanding physical disk capacity without the external network overhead associated with detached block volumes. The primary tradeoff lies in the storage media and single-thread constraints: the local HDDs favor sequential input/output over random low-latency access patterns, while the CPU limits single-threaded execution tasks like rapid compression. The hardware is best suited for big data analytics clusters, distributed file systems, data lakes, batch data processing, and large-scale backup repositories.
description: Amazon Web Services d3en.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance architected for massive local data retention and high-throughput networking. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, it supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth via the Nitro hypervisor. Its key capability is an integrated 223,680 GB local HDD storage array, avoiding detached storage bottlenecks for high-capacity applications. Benchmark evaluations reflect average multi-core and memory throughput alongside lower-tier single-core performance. While unsuitable for latency-sensitive random IOPS due to spinning disk storage, the platform offers exceptional storage density per compute unit. This profile makes it appropriate for distributed file systems, massive data lakes, log aggregation, and sequential data processing pipelines.
